scope: Multiterminal and network information theory source research only.
evidence_basis: Read complete historical author lecture notes arXiv:1001.3404v3 (641 pages), all 24 lectures and Appendices A–E.
Read all pages of the 13 currently hosted Stanford EE376B author slide decks as supplemental sources.

Read complete primary articles Etkin–Tse–Wang arXiv:cs/0702045v2 (52 pages), Wagner–Tavildar–Viswanath arXiv:cs/0510095v3 (55 pages), and Lim–Kim–El Gamal–Chung arXiv:1002.3188v2 (33 pages), including appendices and references.

Read the complete author-hosted final IEEE article Lim–Kim–El Gamal–Chung, Noisy Network Coding, IEEE TIT 57(5), pp. 3132–3152 (May 2011), including Appendices A–G; visually cross-checked final Theorem 4 and the Appendix D matrix-lemma proof against the arXiv v2 version.
Verified public arXiv history for 1001.3404 v1–v5 and directly inspected the one-page v5 notice; v1/v2 were page-count/identity checked but not substantively read, and v4 was not retrieved or read.
handoff_contents: Complete original local finite-alphabet MAC and degraded-broadcast proofs, including operational models, average-error criteria, support-size reductions, and converse/achievability arguments; separate real Gaussian-MAC proof; and exact multicast NNC inner-bound factorization, cut formula, and block-covering/nonunique-packing derivation.

Additional local developments for Ozarow's two-user AWGN feedback MAC, the Gaussian NNC cut-dependent right-side gap and final-journal global vector gap, and the exact relay-feedback topology/cutset capacity; the final paper's signed shift is repaired to a nonnegative clipped vector through active-message NNC packing.
Exact operational models, hypotheses, rate regions, proof routes, Markov/input factorizations, auxiliary cardinalities, closure and error-criterion qualifications.

Precise separation of exact capacity regions from inner/outer bounds and restricted special cases for Slepian–Wolf, MAC, degraded BC, IC, relay/DMN, Gaussian two-encoder lossy coding, feedback and noiseless networks.
Random-coding, typicality, packing, covering, binning and NNC interfaces with local proof obligations.
Existing published library suppliers and their exact scope limitations, plus missing information-theory-specific proofs and interfaces.
limitations: The v3 manuscript is a historical 2010 source, not the later expanded Cambridge book.
The Stanford decks are slide supplements and omit some proof detail; the complete v3 text and full research articles govern claims where they differ.
This lane does not claim an exhaustive 2026 search of every open-problem literature thread; old source statements are not used alone as current-status evidence.

The March 2010 arXiv v2 Theorem 4 states a sharper cut-dependent simultaneous vector allowance but its displayed proof only compares cut right sides; the final 2011 journal version changes the claim to a common 0.63N coordinate shift and supplies a vector construction. Its printed shift can be negative for low-rate coordinates, so the local proof note supplies the active-message positive-part repair; the preprint's sharper vector claim remains unproved here.
The scaffold still has to author each selected definition and proof locally and make its own final supplier/status decisions.
